DiscoveryofBloodCirculation
Pioneers of discovering blood circulation are Ibn al Nafees and William Harvey.
Many other names are also included in the list but these two gave true,
experimentallysupporteddetailsoftheprocess.
Ibn-Al-Nafees(1210-1288)
Blood circulation in human beings was first described
by a Muslim anatomist Ibn-al-Nafees. He studied
medicineatAl-NouriAl-KabeerHospitalinDamascus
Later, he moved to Cairo where he took up medicine
as acareer.Hewas thefirstto explainthepulmonary
blood circulation.He discovered the central role of
the heart in the whole circulatory system.
Furthermore,IbnAl-Nafees explained thatblood was
purified in the lungs.
Fig.9.13:lbn-Al-Nafees
WilliamHarvey(1578-1657)
Harvey was an English physician who was the first in
the Western world to describe correctly the systemic
circulation and properties of blood.Hedemonstrated
that heart and blood vessels form a continuous and
closedsystemofcirculation.
Fig.9.14:WilliamHarvey
9.7 CardiovascularDisorders
The diseases that involve the heart or blood vessels (arteries and veins) are
collectively called cardiovascular disorders.These disorders areone of theleading
causes of death in the world. Heart and arteries are subjected to many types of
damages.Somecommondisordersaregivenbelow.
(i)Atherosclerosis (narrowingofarteries)
It is characterized bythe deposition offatty material e.g.cholesterol inside the
arteries.Due to this deposition,the lumen (interior)of the artery becomes
narrow and blood flows with difficulty.Later,the artery may completely be
blocked.if this blockage is in a coronary artery,it may result in myocardial
infarction.
